chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performed wudu (ablution), then ate meat or fat: may he perform salat (prayer) without washing his hand? He said: Yes. But if it was milk, he should not perform salat (prayer) until he washes his hand and rinses his mouth. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform salat (prayer) after having eaten meat without washing his hand; but if it was milk, he would not perform salat (prayer) until he washed his hand and rinsed his mouth.

What this report contains of the command to wash the hands, rinse the mouth, and inhale water into the nose for one who has drunk milk is to be understood as recommendation, not obligation and requirement, as indicated by the first report.

key_terms.سَمْنًا: fat or clarified butter eaten before salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَبَنًا: milk, after which washing and rinsing are mentioned
key_terms.يَغْسِلَ يَدَهُ: to wash his hand before salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does drinking milk require washing the hands and rinsing the mouth before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on performing salat (prayer) after eating meat, fat, or drinking milk following wudu (ablution). It indicates that washing the hand after eating meat or fat is not required for salat (prayer), while washing the hand and rinsing the mouth after drinking milk is presented in a way that, according to the compiler's note, is understood as recommended rather than obligatory.
